text: Let $9=x_{1}<x_{2}<\ldots <x_{7}$ be in an A.P. with common difference d. If the standard deviation of $x_{1},x_{2}...,x_{7}$ is 4 and the mean is $\bar{x}$, then $\bar{x}+x_{6}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \text{Mean}\Rightarrow \bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{7}x_{i}}{7}=\dfrac{\frac{7}{2}[2a+6d]}{7}=a+3d=x_{4} \\  \\ \text{Variance}=\dfrac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{7}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}}{7}=(4)^{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{7}(x_{i}-x_{4})^{2}}{7}=16 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{(3d)^{2}+(2d)^{2}+d^{2}+0+d^{2}+(2d)^{2}+(3d)^{2}}{7}=16 \\  \\ =4d^{2}=16\Rightarrow d=2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \bar{x}=9+3(2)=15 \\  \\ x_{6}=a+5d=9+5(2)=19\Rightarrow \bar{x}+x_{6}=34 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

$\mathrm{R}_{2}\equiv \mathrm{A}\cup \mathrm{B}–=\mathrm{A}–\cup \mathrm{B}$

$\mathrm{R}_{2}\to$ Reflexive, symmetric

text: The sum of the absolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x)=\left |x^{2}-5x+6\right |-3x+2$ in the interval $[-1,3]$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The sum of the absolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x)=\left |x^{2}-5x+6\right |-3x+2$ in the interval $[-1,3]$ can be found by finding the maximum and minimum values of $f(x)$ in this interval and then adding them.

First, let's find the critical points of $f(x)$. To do this, we will find the zeros of the expression inside the absolute value:

$x^{2}-5x+6=0$

Solving this quadratic equation, we find that the zeros are $x=2$ and $x=3$. These are the critical points of $f(x)$.

Next, we evaluate $f(x)$ at these critical points and at the endpoints of the interval $[-1,3]$:

$f(-1)=\left |(-1)^{2}-5(-1)+6\right |-3(-1)+2=17$

$f(2)=\left |(2)^{2}-5(2)+6\right |-3(2)+2=-4$

$f(3)=\left |(3)^{2}-5(3)+6\right |-3(3)+2=-7$

So, the minimum value of $f(x)$ is $-7$ and the maximum value is $17$.

So, the sum of the absolute maximum and minimum values of the function is $-7+17=10$.

Note : The absolute maximum and minimum values of a function are the largest and smallest values that the function takes on a given interval, respectively. These values are also called the "extrema" of the function. The absolute maximum value is the highest point on the graph of the function, and the absolute minimum value is the lowest point.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: Let $⃗{a}=5\hat{i}-\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $⃗{b}=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ be two vectors. Then which one of the following statements is TRUE ?
options:
Projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}$ is $\frac{-13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction 
of $⃗{b}$.

Projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}$ is $\frac{13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction 
of $⃗{b}$.
Projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}$ is $\frac{13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is same as of $⃗{b}$.
Projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}$ is $\frac{-13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is same as of $⃗{b}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Projection of}⃗{a}\text{on}⃗{b}=\dfrac{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}}{|⃗{b}|} \\  \\ =\dfrac{(5\hat{i}-\hat{j}-3\hat{k})\cdot (\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k})}{\sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}+5^{2}}}=\dfrac{5-3-15}{\sqrt{35}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{-13}{\sqrt{35}} \end{array}$

Negative sign indicates that direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction 
of $⃗{b}$.

text: For the system of linear equations $αx+y+z=1,x+αy+z=1,x+y+αz=β$, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: It has infinitely many solutions if $α=1$ and $β=1$
It has infinitely many solutions if $α=2$ and $β=-1$
It has no solution if $α=-2$ and $β=1$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For infinite solution $\Delta =\Delta _{x}=\Delta _{y}=\Delta _{z}=0$

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} α & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & α & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & α \end{array}\right |=0\Rightarrow \left (α^{3}-3α+2\right )=0\Rightarrow α=1,-2$

If $β=1$, then all planes are overlapping

$\therefore$ Option (A) is correct.

Option (B) :

If $α=2\Rightarrow \Delta \neq 0$

$\therefore$ Unique solution exist

$\therefore$ Option (B) is incorrect.

Option (C) :

$\begin{array}{l} α=2,β=1 \\  \\ 2x+y+z=1 \\  \\ x+2y+z=1 \\  \\ x+y+2z=1 \end{array}$

Adding all three equations,

$x+y+z=\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$ option (C) is correct.

Option (D) :

If $α=-2$ and $β=1$, then $\Delta =0,\Delta _{x}\neq 0$

$\therefore$ No solution.

$\therefore$ Option (D) is correct.

text:
The value of the integral 

$\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{x+\frac{π}{4}}{2-\cos 2x}dx$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\frac{x+\frac{π}{4}}{(2-\cos 2x)}dx$

Using $\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx$

$I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (\frac{-x+\frac{π}{4}}{2-\cos 2x}\right )dx$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore 2I=\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{4}}\dfrac{πdx}{2(2-\cos 2x)} \\  \\ \Rightarrow I=\dfrac{2π}{4}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\dfrac{dx}{2-\frac{1-\tan ^{2}x}{1+\tan ^{2}x}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow I=\dfrac{π}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (\dfrac{1+\tan ^{2}x}{1+3\tan ^{2}x}\right )dx \end{array}$

Now,

$\begin{array}{l} \tan x=t \\  \\ =\dfrac{π}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\dfrac{dt}{1+3t^{2}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{π}{2}\left [\dfrac{\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{3}t)}{\sqrt{3}}\right ]_{0}^{1} \\  \\ =\dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{3}}\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right )=\dfrac{π^{2}}{6\sqrt{3}} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: Let $a,b$ be two real numbers such that $ab<0$. If the complex number $\frac{1+ai}{b+i}$ is of unit modulus and $a+ib$ lies on the circle $|z-1|=|2z|$, then a possible value of $\frac{1+[a]}{4b}$, where $[t]$ is greatest integer function, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \left |\dfrac{1+ai}{b+i}\right |=1 \\  \\ |1+ia|=|b+i| \\  \\ a^{2}+1=b^{2}+1\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\pm \mathrm{b}\Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=-\mathrm{a}\text{as}\mathrm{ab}<0 \\  \\ (\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{ib})\text{lies on}|z-1|=|2z| \\  \\ |a+ib-1|=2|a+ib| \\  \\ (a-1)^{2}+b^{2}=4\left (a^{2}+b^{2}\right ) \\  \\ (a-1)^{2}+a^{2}=4\left (2a^{2}\right ) \\  \\ 1-2a=6a^{2}\Rightarrow 6a^{2}+2a-1=0 \\  \\ a=\dfrac{-2\pm \sqrt{28}}{12}=\dfrac{-1\pm \sqrt{7}}{6} \\  \\ a=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}-1}{6}\text{and}b=\dfrac{1-\sqrt{7}}{6} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} [a]=0 \\  \\ \therefore \dfrac{1+[a]}{4b}=\dfrac{6}{4(1-\sqrt{7})}=-\left (\dfrac{1+\sqrt{7}}{4}\right ) \end{array}$

Similarly when $a=\frac{-1-\sqrt{7}}{6}\text{and}b=\frac{1+\sqrt{7}}{6}$

then [$a$] = -1

$\therefore$ $\frac{1+[a]}{4b}=\frac{1-1}{4\times \frac{1+\sqrt{7}}{6}}$ = 0
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: If $A=\frac{1}{2}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\frac{1}{2}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

Let $θ=\frac{π}{3}$

$\begin{array}{llllll} A^{2} & =\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & \sin θ \\  \\ -\sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & \sin θ \\  \\ -\sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 2θ & \sin 2θ \\  \\ -\sin 2θ & \cos 2θ \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ A^{3} & =\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 2θ & \sin 2θ \\  \\ -\sin 2θ & \cos 2θ \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos θ & \sin θ \\  \\ -\sin θ & \cos θ \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 3θ & \sin 3θ \\  \\ -\sin 3θ & \cos 3θ \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllll} \therefore \quad A^{30}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 30θ & \sin 30θ \\  \\ -\sin 30θ & \cos 30θ \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ A^{25}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \cos 25θ & \sin 25θ \\  \\ -\sin 25θ & \cos 25θ \end{array}\right ]=\dfrac{1}{2}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 \end{array}\right ]=A \\  \\ \therefore \quad A^{30}+A^{25}-A=I \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: Let $αx=\exp \left (x^{β}y^{γ}\right )$ be the solution of the differential equation $2x^{2}y\mathrm{d}y-\left (1-xy^{2}\right )\mathrm{d}x=0,x>0,y(2)=\sqrt{\log _{e}2}$. Then $α+β-γ$ equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 2x^{2}ydy-\left (1-xy^{2}\right )dx=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2x^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx}-1+xy^{2}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{x}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{x}=\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\text{(L.D.E)} \\  \\ Let,y^{2}=t\Rightarrow 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dt}{dx} \\  \\ \dfrac{dt}{dx}+\dfrac{t}{x}=\dfrac{1}{x^{2}} \\  \\ \text{I.F}=e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx}=x \end{array}$

So, the general solution is

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow t\times x=\int x\cdot \dfrac{1}{x^{2}}dx \\  \\ \Rightarrow y^{2}\cdot x=\ln x+c \\  \\ \text{Also,y(2)}=\sqrt{\log _{e}2} \\  \\ \log _{e}^{2}2=\log _{e}2+c\Rightarrow c=\log _{e}2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow y^{2}x=\ln x+\ln 2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow y^{2}x=\ln 2x \\  \\ 2x=\exp \left (x^{1}y^{2}\right ) \end{array}$

By compare it with given solution we get,

$\begin{array}{l} α=2,β=1,γ=2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow α+β-γ=2+1-2=1 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: If the $x$-intercept of a focal chord of the parabola $y^{2}=8x+4y+4$ is 3, then the length of this chord is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y^{2}-4y+4=8x+8\Rightarrow (y-2)^{2}=8(x+1)$, which is $Y^{2}=4aX$ with $X=x+1$, $Y=y-2$ and $a=2$. Its vertex is $(-1,2)$ and its focus is $X=2,Y=0$, i.e. $(1,2)$.

The focal chord passes through $(1,2)$ and through its $x$-intercept $(3,0)$, so its slope is $\dfrac{0-2}{3-1}=-1$ and its equation is $y-2=-(x-1)$, i.e. $Y=2-X$.

Substituting in $Y^{2}=8X$:

$(2-X)^{2}=8X\Rightarrow X^{2}-12X+4=0\Rightarrow X_{1}+X_{2}=12.$

The focal distance of a point of $Y^{2}=4aX$ is $X+a$, so the chord length is

$(X_{1}+a)+(X_{2}+a)=12+4=16.$

Hence, the answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{5^{\cos x}(1+\cos x\cos 3x+\cos ^{2}x+\cos ^{3}x\cos 3x)dx}{1+5^{\cos x}}=\frac{kπ}{16}$, then k is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The bracket factorises:

$1+\cos x\cos 3x+\cos ^{2}x+\cos ^{3}x\cos 3x=(1+\cos ^{2}x)(1+\cos x\cos 3x)=g(x)$

Under $x\to π-x$, both $\cos x$ and $\cos 3x$ change sign, so $\cos ^{2}x$ and $\cos x\cos 3x$ are unchanged and $g(π-x)=g(x)$, while $5^{\cos x}$ becomes $5^{-\cos x}$:

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{5^{-\cos x}g(x)}{1+5^{-\cos x}}dx=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{g(x)}{5^{\cos x}+1}dx$

Adding this to the original form of $I$ gives $2I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}g(x)dx$.

On $[0,π]$: $\int\limits _{0}^{π}dx=π$, $\int\limits _{0}^{π}\cos ^{2}xdx=\dfrac{π}{2}$ and $\int\limits _{0}^{π}\cos x\cos 3xdx=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{π}(\cos 4x+\cos 2x)dx=0$.

With $\cos ^{3}x=\dfrac{3\cos x+\cos 3x}{4}$:

$\int\limits _{0}^{π}\cos ^{3}x\cos 3xdx=\dfrac{3}{4}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\cos x\cos 3xdx+\dfrac{1}{4}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\cos ^{2}3xdx=0+\dfrac{π}{8}$

So $2I=π+\dfrac{π}{2}+\dfrac{π}{8}=\dfrac{13π}{8}$, giving $I=\dfrac{13π}{16}$ and $k=13$.

Hence, the answer is 13.

text: Let the sixth term in the binomial expansion of $\left (\sqrt{2^{\log _{2}(10-3^{x})}}+\sqrt{5 2^{(x-2)\log _{2}3}}\right )^{m}$ in the increasing powers of $2^{(x-2)\log _{2}3}$, be 21 . If the binomial coefficients of the second, third and fourth terms in the expansion are respectively the first, third and fifth terms of an A.P., then the sum of the squares of all possible values of $x$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
${}^{m}C_{1},{}^{m}C_{2},{}^{m}C_{3}$ are first, third and fifth term of $AP$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore  & a={}^{m}C_{1} \\  \\ a+2d={}^{m}C_{2} \\  \\ a+4d={}^{m}C_{3} \\  \\ \therefore  & 2{}^{m}C_{2}-{}^{m}C_{3}=m \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & m=7\text{or}m=2 \\  \\ \because  & m=2\text{is not possible} \\  \\ \therefore  & m=7 \end{array}$

$\mathrm{T}_{6}={}^{\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{C}_{5}(10-3^{\mathrm{x}})^{\frac{\mathrm{m}-5}{2}}\cdot \left (3^{\mathrm{x}-2}\right )=21$

Putting value of m = 7, we get

$\begin{array}{l} T_{5+1}={}^{7}C_{5}(10-3^{x})^{\frac{7-5}{2}}3^{x-2}=21 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{10.3^{x}-(3^{x})^{2}}{3^{2}}=1 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow (3^{x})^{2}-10\cdot 3^{x}+9=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3^{x}=9,1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow x=0,2 \end{array}$

Sum of squares of values of $x = 0^{2} + 2^{2} = 4$

text: If the term without $x$ in the expansion of $\left (x^{\frac{2}{3}}+\frac{α}{x^{3}}\right )^{22}$ is 7315 , then $|α|$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given expansion $\left (x^{\frac{2}{3}}+\frac{α}{x^{3}}\right )^{22}$

$T_{r+1}={}^{22}C_{r}\left (x^{\frac{2}{3}}\right )^{22-r}\left (\frac{α}{x^{3}}\right )^{r}$

For constant term

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{44-2r}{3}-3r=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r=4 \end{array}$

Now ${}^{22}\mathrm{C}_{4}α^{4}=7315$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{22\times 21\times 20\times 19}{4\times 3\times 2\times 1}α^{4}=7315 \\  \\ \therefore α^{4}=1 \\  \\ \therefore |α|=1 \end{array}$
